sanskrit: tam abhyagād bṛhatkṣatraḥ kekayānāṃ mahārathaḥ pravapan niśitān bāṇān mahendrāśanisaṃnibhān
english: Against him advanced Bṛhatkṣatra, the great chariot-warrior of the Kekayas, sowing whetted arrows that resembled the thunderbolt of mighty Indra.

sanskrit: taṃ tu pratyudiyāc chīghraṃ kṣemadhūrtir mahāyaśāḥ vimuñcan niśitān bāṇāñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: But the illustrious Kṣemadhūrti swiftly rose to meet him, loosing whetted arrows by the hundred and by the thousand.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuś ca cedīnām ṛṣabho 'tibaloditaḥ tvarito 'bhyadravad droṇaṃ mahendra iva śambaram
english: And Dhṛṣṭaketu, the bull of the Cedis, risen up in surpassing strength, rushed in haste upon Droṇa as great Indra upon Śambara.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā vyāditāsyam ivāntakam vīradhanvā maheṣvāsas tvaramāṇaḥ samabhyayāt
english: As he bore down all at once, like Death with gaping jaws, the mighty archer Vīradhanvan hastened forth to confront him.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahārāja jigīṣuṃ samavasthitam sahānīkaṃ tato droṇo nyavārayata vīryavān
english: Then, O great king, the valiant Droṇa held back Yudhiṣṭhira, who stood firm with his host, eager for victory.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ kuśalaṃ yuddhe parākrāntaṃ parākramī abhyagacchat samāyāntaṃ vikarṇas te sutaḥ prabho
english: Your valiant son Vikarṇa, O lord, went forth against Nakula, skilled and prowess-filled in battle, as he came on.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ tathāyāntaṃ durmukhaḥ śatrukarśanaḥ śarair anekasāhasraiḥ samavākirad āśugaiḥ
english: And as Sahadeva likewise advanced, Durmukha, the harrier of foes, overwhelmed him with many thousands of swift-flying shafts.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ tu naravyāghraṃ vyāghradattas tv avārayat śaraiḥ suniśitais tīkṣṇaiḥ kampayan vai muhur muhuḥ
english: Vyāghradatta held off Sātyaki, that tiger among men, with keen and sharpened arrows, shaking him again and again.

sanskrit: draupadeyān naravyāghrān muñcataḥ sāyakottamān saṃrabdhān rathināṃ śreṣṭhān saumadattir avārayat
english: Saumadatti held back the sons of Draupadī, those tigers among men, foremost of chariot-warriors, who in their fury loosed their finest shafts.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tathā kruddhaṃ bhīmarūpo bhayānakam pratyavārayad āyāntam ārṣyaśṛṅgir mahārathaḥ
english: And the great chariot-warrior Ārṣyaśṛṅgi, dreadful and fearsome in form, withstood the wrathful Bhīmasena as he came on.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ nararākṣasayor mṛdhe yādṛg eva purā vṛttaṃ rāmarāvaṇayor nṛpa
english: A battle arose between the two of them on the field, that man and that rākṣasa, O king, even such as once took place between Rāma and Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro droṇaṃ navatyā nataparvaṇām ājaghne bharataśreṣṭha sarvamarmasu bhārata
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira struck Droṇa with ninety smooth-jointed arrows in all his vital parts, O best of the Bharatas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaḥ pañcaviṃśatyā nijaghāna stanāntare roṣito bharataśreṣṭha kaunteyena yaśasvinā
english: Droṇa, enraged by the illustrious son of Kuntī, struck him in turn between the breasts with twenty-five shafts, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bhūya eva tu viṃśatyā sāyakānāṃ samācinot sāśvasūtadhvajaṃ droṇaḥ paśyatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: And once more Droṇa covered him over with a score of arrows, together with his horses, charioteer, and banner, before the eyes of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: tāñ śarān droṇamuktāṃs tu śaravarṣeṇa pāṇḍavaḥ avārayata dharmātmā darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: But the righteous son of Pāṇḍu warded off those arrows loosed by Droṇa with a shower of his own, displaying the swiftness of his hand.

sanskrit: tato droṇo bhṛśaṃ kruddho dharmarājasya saṃyuge ciccheda sahasā dhanvī dhanus tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then Droṇa the bowman, exceedingly wroth, suddenly cut asunder in the fray the bow of that high-souled king of righteousness.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ tvaramāṇo mahārathaḥ śarair anekasāhasraiḥ purayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: And as his bow was severed, the great chariot-warrior in haste covered him over on every side with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: adṛśyaṃ dṛśya rājānaṃ bhāradvājasya sāyakaiḥ sarvabhūtāny amanyanta hatam eva yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Seeing the king made invisible by the shafts of Bharadvāja's son, all beings thought Yudhiṣṭhira already slain.

sanskrit: ke cic cainam amanyanta tathā vai vimukhīkṛtam hṛto rājeti rājendra brāhmaṇena yaśasvinā
english: Some thought him thus turned away in flight: "The king is carried off," O lord of kings, "by the illustrious brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: sa kṛcchraṃ paramaṃ prāpto dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tyaktvā tat kārmukaṃ chinnaṃ bhāradvājena saṃyuge ādade 'nyad dhanur divyaṃ bhāraghnaṃ vegavattaram
english: The king of righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, fallen into the utmost extremity, cast aside that bow cut down by Bharadvāja's son in the fray and took up another, a celestial bow, burden-crushing and swifter still.

sanskrit: tatas tān sāyakān sarvān droṇamuktān sahasraśaḥ ciccheda samare vīras tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then the hero cut to pieces in the battle all those arrows loosed by Droṇa by the thousand, and it was as a marvel to behold.

sanskrit: chittvā ca tāñ śarān rājā krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ śaktiṃ jagrāha samare girīṇām api dāraṇīm svarṇadaṇḍāṃ mahāghorām aṣṭaghaṇṭāṃ bhayāvahām
english: And having cut those shafts apart, the king, his eyes red with wrath, seized in the battle a spear that could rend even mountains, gold-shafted, most terrible, hung with eight bells, and dread to behold.

sanskrit: samutkṣipya ca tāṃ hṛṣṭo nanāda balavad balī nādena sarvabhūtāni trāsayann iva bhārata
english: And raising it aloft in his joy, the mighty one roared with a great roar, as if terrifying all beings with that cry, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ samudyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmarājena saṃyuge svasti droṇāya sahasā sarvabhūtāny athābruvan
english: Seeing the spear uplifted by the king of righteousness in the fray, all beings cried out at once, "Hail to Droṇa! May it be well with Droṇa!"

sanskrit: sā rājabhujanirmuktā nirmuktoragasaṃnibhā prajvālayantī gaganaṃ diśaś ca vidiśas tathā droṇāntikam anuprāptā dīptāsyā pannagī yathā
english: Loosed from the king's arm, like a serpent that has cast its slough, blazing across the sky and the quarters and the intermediate quarters, it drew near to Droṇa like a flaming-mouthed she-snake.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā prekṣya droṇo viśāṃ pate prāduścakre tato brāhmam astram astravidāṃ varaḥ
english: Seeing it bearing down upon him all at once, O lord of peoples, Droṇa, the best of those versed in weapons, brought forth the brāhma weapon.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ bhasmasāt kṛtvā tāṃ śaktiṃ ghoradarśanām jagāma syandanaṃ tūrṇaṃ pāṇḍavasya yaśasvinaḥ
english: That weapon reduced to ashes the spear of dreadful aspect and sped swiftly toward the chariot of the illustrious son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā droṇāstraṃ tat samudyatam aśāmayan mahāprājño brahmāstreṇaiva bhārata
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, exceedingly wise, quelled that uplifted weapon of Droṇa with the brahma weapon itself, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vivyādha ca raṇe droṇaṃ pañcabhir nataparvabhiḥ kṣurapreṇa ca tīkṣṇena cicchedāsya mahad dhanuḥ
english: And he pierced Droṇa in the fight with five smooth-jointed shafts, and with a sharp razor-headed arrow cut asunder his great bow.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ droṇaḥ kṣatriyamardanaḥ gadāṃ cikṣepa sahasā dharmaputrāya māriṣa
english: Casting aside that severed bow, Droṇa, the crusher of kṣatriyas, suddenly hurled a mace at the son of Dharma, O worthy one.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā gadāṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ gadām evāgrahīt kruddhaś cikṣepa ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: Seeing that mace bearing down on him all at once, Yudhiṣṭhira, scorcher of foes, in his wrath seized a mace of his own and hurled it.

sanskrit: te gade sahasā mukte samāsādya parasparam saṃgharṣāt pāvakaṃ muktvā sameyātāṃ mahītale
english: Those two maces, suddenly loosed, met each other and, striking out fire from their collision, came together upon the ground.

sanskrit: tato droṇo bhṛśaṃ kruddho dharmarājasya māriṣa caturbhir niśitais tīkṣṇair hayāñ jaghne śarottamaiḥ
english: Then Droṇa, exceedingly enraged, O worthy one, slew the horses of the king of righteousness with four keen and sharpened, choicest shafts.

sanskrit: dhanuś caikena bāṇena cicchedendradhvajopamam ketum ekena ciccheda pāṇḍavaṃ cārdayat tribhiḥ
english: With a single arrow he cut his bow, and with one he severed his banner that rose like Indra's standard, and with three he tormented the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tasthāv ūrdhvabhujo rājā vyāyudho bharatarṣabha
english: Leaping down swiftly from his chariot with its slain horses, King Yudhiṣṭhira stood with arms upraised, weaponless, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: virathaṃ taṃ samālokya vyāyudhaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ droṇo vyamohayac chatrūn sarvasainyāni cābhibho
english: Beholding him bereft of his chariot and weaponless besides, Droṇa threw the foes and all their armies into confusion, O lord.

sanskrit: muñcann iṣugaṇāṃs tīkṣṇāṃl laghuhasto dṛḍhavrataḥ abhidudrāva rājānaṃ siṃho mṛgam ivolbaṇaḥ
english: Loosing volleys of sharp arrows, swift of hand and firm of vow, he rushed upon the king as a fierce lion upon a deer.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutam ālokya droṇenāmitraghātinā hā heti sahasā śabdaḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ samajāyata
english: Seeing him thus assailed by Droṇa, the slayer of foes, a sudden cry of "Alas! Alas!" arose all at once among the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: hṛto rājā hṛto rājā bhāradvājena māriṣa ity āsīt sumahāñ śabdaḥ pāṇḍusainyasya sarvataḥ
english: "The king is carried off, the king is carried off by Bharadvāja's son!" O worthy one, such was the mighty clamor that rose on every side from the army of the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tatas tvaritam āruhya sahadevarathaṃ nṛpaḥ apāyāj javanair aśvaiḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, swiftly mounting Sahadeva's chariot, withdrew with its fleet horses.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bṛhatkṣatram athāyāntaṃ kekayaṃ dṛḍhavikramam kṣemadhūrtir mahārāja vivyādhorasi mārgaṇaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As Bṛhatkṣatra the Kekaya, firm in valor, came on, Kṣemadhūrti, O great king, pierced him in the breast with arrows.

sanskrit: bṛhatkṣatras tu taṃ rājā navatyā nataparvaṇām ājaghne tvarito yuddhe droṇānīkabibhitsayā
english: But King Bṛhatkṣatra, eager in the fight to breach Droṇa's array, swiftly struck him with ninety smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: kṣemadhūrtis tu saṃkruddhaḥ kekayasya mahātmanaḥ dhanuś ciccheda bhallena pītena niśitena ca
english: But Kṣemadhūrti, greatly enraged, cut asunder the bow of the high-souled Kekaya with a sharp, yellow-burnished broad-headed arrow.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ śareṇa nataparvaṇā vivyādha hṛdaye tūrṇaṃ pravaraṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: And as his bow was severed, he swiftly pierced in the heart with a smooth-jointed shaft that foremost of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya bṛhatkṣatro hasann iva vyaśvasūtadhvajaṃ cakre kṣemadhūrtiṃ mahāratham
english: Then taking up another bow, Bṛhatkṣatra, as if with a smile, stripped the great chariot-warrior Kṣemadhūrti of his horses, charioteer, and banner.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena pītena niśitena ca jahāra nṛpateḥ kāyāc chiro jvalitakuṇḍalam
english: Then with another sharp, yellow-burnished broad-headed arrow he severed from the king's body his head with its blazing earrings.

sanskrit: tac chinnaṃ sahasā tasya śiraḥ kuñcitamūrdhajam sakirīṭaṃ mahīṃ prāpya babhau jyotir ivāmbarāt
english: That head of his, suddenly severed, with its curling locks and its diadem, falling to the earth, shone like a star fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya raṇe hṛṣṭo bṛhatkṣatro mahārathaḥ sahasābhyapatat sainyaṃ tāvakaṃ pārthakāraṇāt
english: Having slain him in battle, the great chariot-warrior Bṛhatkṣatra, exultant, fell suddenly upon your host for the sake of the sons of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketum athāyāntaṃ droṇahetoḥ parākramī vīradhanvā maheṣvāso vārayām āsa bhārata
english: And as Dhṛṣṭaketu came on, the valiant mighty archer Vīradhanvan held him back for Droṇa's sake, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tau parasparam āsādya śaradaṃṣṭrau tarasvinau śarair anekasāhasrair anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Closing with each other, those two swift warriors, their teeth as arrows, struck one another with many thousands of shafts.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau naraśārdūlau yuyudhāte parasparam mahāvane tīvramadau vāraṇāv iva yūthapau
english: Those two tigers among men fought with each other like two leader-elephants of the herd, fierce with rut, in a great forest.

sanskrit: girigahvaram āsādya śārdūlāv iva roṣitau yuyudhāte mahāvīryau parasparajighāṃsayā
english: Like two enraged tigers met within a mountain cavern, those two mighty heroes fought, each seeking to slay the other.

sanskrit: tad yuddham āsīt tumulaṃ prekṣaṇīyaṃ viśāṃ pate siddhacāraṇasaṃghānāṃ vismayādbhutadarśanam
english: That battle was tumultuous and worth the beholding, O lord of peoples, a marvelous and wondrous sight for the throngs of Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: vīradhanvā tataḥ kruddho dhṛṣṭaketoḥ śarāsanam dvidhā ciccheda bhallena prahasann iva bhārata
english: Then Vīradhanvan, enraged, cut Dhṛṣṭaketu's bow in two with a broad-headed arrow, as if with a laugh, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad utsṛjya dhanuś chinnaṃ cedirājo mahārathaḥ śaktiṃ jagrāha vipulāṃ rukmadaṇḍām ayasmayīm
english: Casting aside that severed bow, the great chariot-warrior, king of the Cedis, seized a broad spear, gold-shafted and wrought of iron.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu śaktiṃ mahāvīryāṃ dorbhyām āyamya bhārata cikṣepa sahasā yatto vīradhanvarathaṃ prati
english: Drawing back that mighty spear with both arms, O Bhārata, he hurled it all at once, with full effort, against the chariot of Vīradhanvan.

sanskrit: sa tayā vīraghātinyā śaktyā tv abhihato bhṛśam nirbhinnahṛdayas tūrṇaṃ nipapāta rathān mahīm
english: Struck hard by that hero-slaying spear, his heart pierced through, he swiftly fell from his chariot to the earth.

sanskrit: tasmin vinihate śūre trigartānāṃ mahārathe balaṃ te 'bhajyata vibho pāṇḍaveyaiḥ samantataḥ
english: When that hero, the great chariot-warrior of the Trigartas, was slain, your force was broken on every side by the Pāṇḍavas, O lord.

sanskrit: sahadeve tataḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ sāyakān durmukho 'kṣipat nanāda ca mahānādaṃ tarjayan pāṇḍavaṃ raṇe
english: Then Durmukha cast sixty arrows at Sahadeva and roared a great roar, threatening the son of Pāṇḍu in the fray.

sanskrit: madreyas tu tataḥ kruddho durmukhaṃ daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ bhrātā bhrātaram āyāntaṃ vivyādha prahasann iva
english: Then the son of Mādrī, enraged, pierced the oncoming Durmukha with ten arrows, brother piercing brother, as if with a laugh.

sanskrit: taṃ raṇe rabhasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahadevaṃ mahābalam durmukho navabhir bāṇais tāḍayām āsa bhārata
english: Seeing the mighty Sahadeva impetuous in battle, Durmukha smote him with nine arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: durmukhasya tu bhallena chittvā ketuṃ mahābalaḥ jaghāna caturo vāhāṃś caturbhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But the mighty Sahadeva, having cut down Durmukha's banner with a broad-headed arrow, slew his four steeds with four whetted shafts.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena pītena niśitena ca ciccheda sāratheḥ kāyāc chiro jvalitakuṇḍalam
english: And with another sharp, yellow-burnished broad-headed arrow he severed from the charioteer's body his head with its blazing earrings.

sanskrit: kṣurapreṇa ca tīkṣṇena kauravyasya mahad dhanuḥ sahadevo raṇe chittvā taṃ ca vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: And with a sharp razor-headed arrow Sahadeva cut asunder in the fight the great bow of the Kaurava and pierced him with five shafts.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ tu rathaṃ tyaktvā durmukho vimanās tadā āruroha rathaṃ rājan niramitrasya bhārata
english: Then Durmukha, dejected, abandoning his chariot with its slain horses, mounted the chariot of Niramitra, O king, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sahadevas tataḥ kruddho niramitraṃ mahāhave jaghāna pṛtanāmadhye bhallena paravīrahā
english: Then Sahadeva, the slayer of hostile heroes, in his wrath struck down Niramitra in the great battle, in the midst of the host, with a broad-headed arrow.

sanskrit: sa papāta rathopasthān niramitro janeśvaraḥ trigartarājasya suto vyathayaṃs tava vāhinīm
english: Niramitra, lord of men, son of the king of the Trigartas, fell from the floor of his chariot, troubling your host as he fell.

sanskrit: taṃ tu hatvā mahābāhuḥ sahadevo vyarocata yathā dāśarathī rāmaḥ kharaṃ hatvā mahābalam
english: Having slain him, the mighty-armed Sahadeva shone forth as Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, when he had slain the mighty Khara.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīt trigartānāṃ janeśvara rājaputraṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā niramitraṃ mahābalam
english: A great cry of dismay arose among the Trigartas, O lord of men, when they saw the mighty prince Niramitra slain.

sanskrit: nakulas te sutaṃ rājan vikarṇaṃ pṛthulocanam muhūrtāj jitavān saṃkhye tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Nakula, O king, overcame your son Vikarṇa of the large eyes in battle within a moment, and it was as a marvel.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ vyāghradattas tu śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ cakre 'dṛśyaṃ sāśvasūtaṃ sadhvajaṃ pṛtanāntare
english: But Vyāghradatta made Sātyaki, together with his horses, charioteer, and banner, invisible amid the host with smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tān nivārya śarāñ śūraḥ śaineyaḥ kṛtahastavat sāśvasūtadhvajaṃ bāṇair vyāghradattam apātayat
english: Warding off those arrows, the hero, the grandson of Śini, with the skill of a master hand, brought down Vyāghradatta with his shafts, together with his horses, charioteer, and banner.

sanskrit: kumāre nihate tasmin magadhasya sute prabho māgadhāḥ sarvato yattā yuyudhānam upādravan
english: When that prince, the son of the king of Magadha, was slain, O lord, the men of Magadha, straining on every side, rushed upon Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: visṛjantaḥ śarāṃś caiva tomarāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ bhiṇḍipālāṃs tathā prāsān mudgarān musalān api
english: Hurling by the thousand arrows and lances, slings and javelins, maces and pestles as well,

sanskrit: ayodhayan raṇe śūrāḥ sātvataṃ yuddhadurmadam tāṃs tu sarvān sa balavān sātyaktir yuddhadurmadaḥ nātikṛcchrād dhasann eva vijigye puruṣarṣabha
english: those heroes did battle in the fray with the Sātvata, mad for combat; but the mighty Sātyaki, himself mad for combat, vanquished them all without great trouble, as if with a laugh, O bull among men.

sanskrit: māgadhān dravato dṛṣṭvā hataśeṣān samantataḥ balaṃ te 'bhajyata vibho yuyudhānaśarārditam
english: Seeing the men of Magadha, those who survived the slaughter, fleeing on every side, your force, tormented by the arrows of Yuyudhāna, was broken, O lord.

sanskrit: nāśayitvā raṇe sainyaṃ tvadīyaṃ mādhavottamaḥ vidhunvāno dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ vyabhrājata mahāyaśāḥ
english: Having destroyed your host in the fight, the illustrious chief of the Mādhavas shone forth, brandishing his excellent bow.

sanskrit: bhajyamānaṃ balaṃ rājan sātvatena mahātmanā nābhyavartata yuddhāya trāsitaṃ dīrghabāhunā
english: The force being broken, O king, by the high-souled Sātvata, terrified by the long-armed hero, did not turn back to the battle.

sanskrit: tato droṇo bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ sahasodvṛtya cakṣuṣī sātyakiṃ satyakarmāṇaṃ svayam evābhidudruve
english: Then Droṇa, exceedingly enraged, his eyes suddenly rolling, himself rushed upon Sātyaki of the truthful deeds.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca draupadeyān maheṣvāsān saumadattir mahāyaśāḥ ekaikaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: The illustrious Saumadatti, having pierced each of the mighty-archer sons of Draupadī with five arrows, pierced them again with seven.
